paper.title: A stochastic proximal alternating method for non-smooth non-convex optimization

problem.finite_sum_components: F_j(U,V)=||U v_j-M[:,j]||_2^2/(2*m), F=(1/n)sum_j F_j; n=image count
problem.V_domain: entrywise_l1_norm(V)<=s and spectral_norm(V)<=RV; V is SIGNED
problem.adaptation_label: Convex-constraint adaptation of a published factorization benchmark, NOT verbatim reproduction of SPRING sparse-NMF Eq.5.1
problem.published_difference: Published sparse-NMF requires both factors nonnegative and hard l0 column sparsity; this experiment uses a convex l1 ball on signed V and compact spectral caps

assumption_audit.A1: J and R are indicators of nonempty compact convex intersections; proper, lower semicontinuous and bounded below by zero
assumption_audit.A2: Each component is a quartic polynomial; its joint gradient is Lipschitz on bounded sets. All iterates and mixed block points remain in the spectral product domain
assumption_audit.A3: Global partial smoothness for fixed opposite block holds; on C, Lx<=RV^2/m and Ly<=RU^2/m
assumption_audit.A4: The constrained squared-error objective is bounded below by zero
assumption_audit.global_smooth_extension_comment: SPRING only assumes locally Lipschitz joint gradients, unlike the literal global SFRAMES manuscript assumption
assumption_audit.additional_KL_or_error_bound_claim: None. No global-optimum, linear-rate, or KL-exponent claim is made

theorem_mode.step_schedule: Constant, positive, nonincreasing; strictly below 1/(4Lx) and 1/(4Ly)
theorem_mode.mini_batch: Fresh uniform fixed-size subsets WITHOUT replacement, separately sampled for U and V blocks
theorem_mode.initialization: Common supplied feasible factors; exact full-gradient initialization for each block at its first query point
theorem_mode.output: Uniform random pre-update iterate alpha in 0,...,T-1; expected squared distance to generalized block gradient mapping G_(gamma_u/2,gamma_v/2) from Eq1.4
theorem_mode.output_warning: Loss plots, last iterates and a common joint projected-gradient residual are useful diagnostics but are not the exact theorem statistic. Eq1.4 evaluates the V gradient at the updated U block
theorem_mode.oracle_count: n component-gradient calls per full callback; 2b per recursive block difference. A complete alternating nonrefresh step costs 4b; initialization costs 2n

practical_mode.label: SPRING-SARAH practical constant component-bound control; NOT theorem-prescribed and NOT verbatim published practical setting
practical_mode.published_setting: Section5.1 uses 1/(2*L_tilde_block), where five power iterations on a sampled batch estimate local partial Lipschitz constants
practical_mode.published_theory_mismatch: Remark5.1 explicitly says experimental steps replace the conservative Section3/4 theoretical prescriptions

proximal_oracle.algorithm: Exact one-set reduction when either single-set projection is feasible for the other set; Dykstra splitting only when both constraints are coupled
proximal_oracle.feasible_candidate: Last side-constraint projection followed by inward radial spectral rescaling, which preserves the side constraint
proximal_oracle.orthant_support: 0 if every entry of q<=0; otherwise infinity
proximal_oracle.exact_arithmetic_certificate: For a primal-feasible candidate c, ||c-proj_intersection(z)||_F <= sqrt(2*(0.5||c-z||_F^2-d(p,q)))
proximal_oracle.requested_distance: 1e-8/(outer_iteration+1)^1.1 by default; a summable ideal target
proximal_oracle.roundoff_handling: Extended-precision accumulation, direct and stable dual-gap forms, a reported rounding allowance scaled by thin matrix rank, objective/support magnitudes AND absolute input/candidate squared norms. The absolute scales cover subtraction in corrections p/q and dual input products when corrections are tiny; floor dominance is recorded as numerical_floor
proximal_oracle.iteration_cap: 2000 Dykstra iterations by default; ProjectionFailure raised unless the numerical gap target is attained
proximal_oracle.limitation: This is a controlled numerical approximation to the exact proximal oracle. A summable requested tolerance does not establish an inexact SPRING theorem, and the floating-point floor is not summable. The parameter prescription is paper-matched; the numerical proximal implementation is not claimed literally exact

validation.independent_projection_check: CVXPY/CLARABEL small spectral-intersection conic programs for both orthant and signed entrywise-l1 cases; primal objectives and dual lower bounds compared
other_checks: Full-batch SARAH recursion agrees with exact alternating gradient updates, including mixed V query points
Checkpoint round-trip preserves both gradient histories and RNG state bitwise
Without-replacement block sampling and oracle accounting
Explicit cap failures and non-exact numerical-floor metadata
Tiny active-l1 corrections terminate using the mathematically exact one-set reduction instead of exhausting the iteration cap
Spectral-only reduction agrees with analytic rank-one projection
validation.last_result: 10 baseline tests and 2 runner integration tests passed; one independent CLARABEL solve reports optimal_inaccurate at the requested 1e-11 solver tolerances, while objective/duality checks pass
